title: Expose bounded parent-visible activity for a running delegated child
outcome: A delegation's owning parent can inspect bounded host-observed activity for the current child attempt before a terminal result exists, without mistaking lack of observation for a stalled reviewer or changing the child's execution.
acceptance: A parent-authorized activity read for a running child reports the current attempt/runtime scope, observation time, last observed activity time and kind, and available observed tool/command counts with their coverage. Missing or unsupported observations are explicit unknowns, not invented zero counts. It never exposes raw prompts, command arguments, output or secrets.

The activity observation is harness-agnostic and performs no resume, cancellation, replacement, retry or completion. Polls do not advance the child's activity time. Restart, runtime replacement and follow-up attempts cannot attribute a prior attempt's activity to the current one. Existing status refresh semantics, if reused, are documented rather than described as side-effect-free.

Focused tests prove parent isolation, running-child visibility, absent-telemetry behavior, correct observed activity updates, stale-attempt exclusion and unchanged child execution. The maintained full gate and required independent review pass on the exact input; documentation states that inactivity observations alone do not establish a stall.
